name: HAZUS highway bridges
source: FEMA, Hazus Earthquake Model Technical Manual, Hazus 6.1, July 2024, Section 7.1 (Tables 7-1, 7-2 and 7-6; Equations 7-1 to 7-4)
intensity_measure_also_needed: SA(0.3) for the Kshape factor, classes with ishape = 1

adjustments.k_3d: 1 + A / (N - B), N = number of spans
adjustments.slight: median * min(1, k_shape) if ishape = 1, else median

assumptions: Seismic design cutoff: Table 7-1 is followed (1975 in California, 1990 elsewhere). The sentence above the table in the Hazus 6.1 manual states the two years the other way round; the table matches earlier Hazus documentation.

K3D = 1 + A / (N - B), as given in Table 7-2 and the text. Equation 7-3 is typeset as (1 + A) / (N - B), but the manual's worked example evaluates it to 1.125 for A = 0.25, B = 1, N = 3, which is the Table 7-2 form.
Where N - B is zero or negative (a single-span bridge with an equation that has B = 1), K3D is taken as 1. The manual does not say what to do in this case.
HWB28 has no K3D equation or Ishape entry in Table 7-1; K3D is taken as 1 and Kshape is not applied.
Number of spans N is NBI Item 45 (main unit spans), as in the manual's example.
'Length less than 20 m' is evaluated on NBI Item 49 (structure length).
A skew coded 99 in the NBI (skew varies along the bridge) is evaluated as 45 degrees. The manual does not address this code. A value of 90 or more is otherwise treated as 0.
Only ground shaking is evaluated. Ground-failure (permanent ground deformation) damage needs a displacement hazard layer.
